newsitem.title: INDIA: Three hurt in grenade blast at holy Kashmir shrine.
newsitem.headline: Three hurt in grenade blast at holy Kashmir shrine.

text.p: A grenade exploded outside Kashmir Valley's holiest shrine on Friday, injuring three people and alarming thousands of praying Moslems, police said.

Suspected separatist guerrillas hurled the grenade at a paramilitary picket just outside the Hazratbal shrine, 13 km (eight miles) southeast of Srinagar, the summer capital of India's northern Jammu and Kashmir state.
A girl and two paramilitary officers were injured when the grenade exploded 100 metres (yards) from the shrine gate, police said. They were taken to hospital for treatment.
More than 100,000 Kashmiris had gathered to pray at Hazratbal on the Friday following the Moslem Shab-e-Mehraj festival, police said.

More than 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year revolt in Kashmir. Dozens of militant groups opposed to Indian rule in the Himalayan region are fighting for either independence or merger with Pakistan.
